 Per: Justice Jai Kumar Pillai :
 Order

This intra-court appeal under Section 2(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Uchcha Nyayalaya (Khand Nyaya Peeth Ko Appeal) Adhiniyam, 2005, invokes the appellate jurisdiction of this Court to assail the impugned order dated 25.08.2025 passed by the learned Single Judge in W.P. No.25524/2024.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Uchcha Nyayalaya (Khand Nyaya Peeth Ko Appeal) Adhiniyam, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: By the said order, the learned Single Judge has dismissed the writ petition preferred by the Appellant against his termination from service.

2. The brief facts leading to the filing of the present appeal, as emerging from the record, are that the Appellant was initially appointed on 04.07.2012 to the post of Constable (Driver) under Respondent No.2, Superintendent of Police, Dewas, and was allotted the rank of Constable No.536.
3.
Prior to his appointment, the Appellant had solemnized marriage with Smt. Pratibha Chouhan on 09.05.2006.
Owing to matrimonial discord, the Appellant's wife resided separately at her parental home and initiated multiple criminal complaints against the Appellant and his family members.

Among these, Crime NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:5889 No.13/2009 (under Sections 498A, 323, 506 of the IPC) and Crime No.309/2008 (under Sections 324, 294, 506, 279,
and 34 of the IPC) were registered.
The latter case was disposed of on 31.03.2011 by the learned JMFC, Dhar, prior to the Appellant's appointment in service.

4. An enquiry was conducted by respondent No.2 on 21.02.2014, which categorically exonerated the Appellant of the allegations of a second marriage, concluding that the complaints were motivated by family disputes and that the alleged second wife, Smt. Pinky Chouhan, was the legally wedded wife of the Appellant's younger brother.
Despite this exonerating report, departmental proceedings were initiated against the Appellant, resulting in the termination of his services.
5. The Appellant's departmental appeal and subsequent mercy/review petition were dismissed by the competent authorities on 23.08.2016 and 16.03.2017, respectively.

Thereafter, on 28.06.2022,
the Appellant was acquitted of the offences under Sections 498-A and 506-B of the IPC by the learned JMFC, Indore.
Subsequently, a decree of divorce was granted on 06.09.2022.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:5889 6.
Relying upon his acquittal, the appellant submitted a representation dated 06.02.2024 seeking reinstatement, which was rejected on 19.04.2024.

Aggrieved, the appellant preferred W.P.
No.25524/2024, which came to be dismissed by the learned Single Judge vide the impugned order Upendra Singh Chouhan vs State Of M.P. on 27 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64452357/
2 dated 25.08.2025.
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the learned Single Judge failed to appreciate the departmental enquiry report dated 21.02.2014, which explicitly exonerated the Appellant from the allegations of a second marriage.

8. It was further contended that the extreme penalty of removal from service is grossly disproportionate and violates the Doctrine of Proportionality, as well as Police Regulations 226(iii)
and 226(v).

The appellant placed reliance on Police Regulation 241, arguing that it mandates reinstatement following an acquittal from criminal charges.
9.

The appellant additionally urged that the departmental proceedings were vitiated by a denial of the principles of natural justice, including the non-supply of material documents and denial of defence assistance.

It was submitted that the foundation of the departmental punishment collapsed upon the appellant's subsequent NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:5889 acquittal and divorce, rendering the termination malicious, discriminatory, and arbitrary.

10. Per contra, the stand of the respondents, as emerging from the record and the findings of the learned Single Judge, is that the appellant's services were terminated on the specific ground of suppression of material information and misrepresentation in the verification form and affidavit submitted at the threshold of his employment.
11. The respondents contended that the appellant, in his verification form and affidavit dated 28.01.2012, falsely declared himself as unmarried and suppressed the fact that he had children.

Furthermore, the appellant explicitly concealed the registration of a criminal case against him (Crime No.309/08) by filling "nil" in the relevant columns and submitting a sworn affidavit declaring that no criminal case was registered or pending against him.

12. It was the specific case of the respondents that the appellant, entering a disciplined police force,
was required to possess an impeccable character.
Such gross suppression of material facts renders him unfit for the post.

The respondents supported their action under Rule 53(C) and Regulation 57 of the M.P. Police NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:5889 Regulations, asserting that a subsequent acquittal does not absolve the appellant of the independent and grave misconduct of suppressing material facts to secure employment.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 13. Having heard the rival contentions and perused the record, this Court finds that the core issue revolves around the suppression of material facts by the appellant at the time of seeking employment.
14. A perusal of the impugned order reveals that the learned Single Judge has meticulously examined the verification form and the affidavit dated 28.01.2012 submitted by the appellant.
The documentary evidence unequivocally demonstrates that the appellant, despite being married and having children, declared himself as unmarried.

More crucially, the appellant suppressed the registration of Crime No.309/08 and falsely swore on affidavit that no criminal case had ever been Upendra Singh Chouhan vs State Of M.P. on 27 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64452357/
3 registered against him.

entities.text: Upendra Singh Chouhan vs State Of M.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These specific charges of suppression and misrepresentation were duly proved during the departmental enquiry.

15. The law is well-settled, as rightly relied upon by the learned Single Judge in light of the binding precedents of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, including the mandate in Avtar Singh v. Union of India,
(2016) 8 SCC 471 that a candidate seeking recruitment to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:5889 the police service must be a person of utmost rectitude and impeccable character.

entities.text:
Avtar Singh v. Union of India,
(2016) 8 SCC 471
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The deliberate suppression of material information regarding criminal antecedents,
marital status, and children at the very threshold of entering a disciplined force constitutes a grave misconduct in itself.

The subsequent acquittal in the criminal cases or the dissolution of marriage does not cure, mitigate, or obliterate the initial fraud and suppression committed by the appellant to secure the employment.
16. The findings recorded by the learned Single Judge are based on a proper appreciation of the material on record and the settled position of law.

The action taken by the respondents in terminating the services of the appellant upon discovery of such suppression does not suffer from any illegality, arbitrariness, or violation of statutory rules.
17. Consequently, this Court does not find any perversity, illegality, or jurisdictional error in the impugned order dated 25.08.2025 passed in W.P. No.25524/2024.
The view taken by the learned Single Judge is eminently just and proper, warranting no interference in this intra-court appeal.
Therefore, the order of the learned Single Judge is hereby upheld.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:5889 18.
Ex- consequenti, the writ appeal, being devoid of merit, stands dismissed.
19. No order as to costs.
20. Pending applications, if any, shall be disposed of accordingly.
